subproblem.title: On a Borel subset of a coordinate n-plane, an IM orientation is a Borel sign times the coordinate n-vector (parent steps 9-10)
subproblem.statement: Assume (IMC-b) [the second conjunct of the frozen hypothesis (IMC) of the parent]: for all P, n, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R in U and every set E, if U is open and E is Borel then there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with R' representing A, R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient, and (PO) [the exact frozen type of the sibling Submission.cmcdtfr_plane_orientation]: for all P, n, strictly increasing ι : Fin n → Fin P, A ⊆ ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, linear subspaces Q ⊆ ℝ^P and n-vectors ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P n, if a_i = x_i for every a ∈ A and every i ∉ range ι, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, then either ξ(α) = α(E_ι) for every n-covector α or ξ(α) = −α(E_ι) for every α, where E_ι := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}). Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U (IMRep U n), ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing, c ∈ ℝ^P and E ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set lying in the coordinate plane through c spanned by e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}: a_i = c_i for every a ∈ E and every i ∉ range ι. Then there is a Borel function σ : ℝ^P → ℤ with |σ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x such that, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E (i.e. μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ E)-a.e.), ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(E_ι) for every n-covector α.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (ι : Fin n → Fin P) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n), StrictMono ι → (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ i, (∀ j, ι j ≠ i) → a i = x i) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))) ∨ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = -α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)))) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (ι : Fin n → Fin P) (c : Euclid P) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → StrictMono ι → MeasurableSet E → (∀ a ∈ E, ∀ i, (∀ j, ι j ≠ i) → a i = c i) → ∃ σ : Euclid P → ℤ, Measurable σ ∧ (∀ x, |σ x| ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ E)), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, R.orient x α = (σ x : ℝ) * α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof (orientation on a face: (IMC)(b) and plane_orientation give ξ = ±e_ι a.e.) together with the Borel sign function of step 10 (σ read off from a strongly measurable version of ξ), written for a general Borel set E in a coordinate plane and a general open U.

Notation: E_ι := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}), e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1; Hⁿ := μHE[n].

1. (Restriction to E.) U is open and E is Borel, so (IMC-b) applied to P, n, U, R, E gives A and R' : IMRep U n with R'.carrier = M ∩ E and R'.orient = ξ. The field R'.orients, rewritten with these equalities, says: for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.
2. (Sign a.e.) M ∩ E is Borel (R.measurableSet_carrier, E Borel), so Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ E (ae_restrict_mem). Take x satisfying this and step 1, with its Q. For every a ∈ M ∩ E and every i with ι(j) ≠ i for all j: a_i = c_i (a ∈ E) and x_i = c_i (x ∈ E), so a_i = x_i. Hence (PO) applies to (P, n, ι, A := M ∩ E, x, Q, ξ(x)) and yields: ξ(x)(α) = α(E_ι) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(E_ι) for all α. This holds for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x.
3. (A Borel version of ξ.) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient). Let ξ̃ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk ξ; it is strongly measurable and ξ = ξ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., hence also Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. since M ∩ E ⊆ M (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
4. (The coordinate n-vector.) Let e ∈ MultiVector P n be evaluation at E_ι, e(α) := α(E_ι); it is the continuous linear functional ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ E_ι.
5. (The sign.) Define σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃(x) = e; σ(x) := −1 if ξ̃(x) ≠ e and ξ̃(x) = −e; σ(x) := 0 otherwise. Clearly |σ(x)| ≤ 1. The sets {x : ξ̃(x) = e} and {x : ξ̃(x) = −e} are Borel because ξ̃ and the constant maps are strongly measurable into a metrizable space (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun). Hence σ is Borel (Measurable.ite twice, constants measurable).
   Formalization note: instance search does not find TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) for the ContinuousLinearMap topology. Supply it locally as ⟨⟨m.toUniformSpace, rfl, @EMetric.instIsCountablyGeneratedUniformity _ m.toPseudoEMetricSpace⟩⟩ with m : PseudoMetricSpace (MultiVector P n) := inferInstance; T0Space (MultiVector P n) is found automatically.
6. (Conclusion.) For Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x both step 2 and ξ(x) = ξ̃(x) hold. Fix such x and α.
   (a) If ξ(x)(β) = β(E_ι) for all β, then ξ(x) = e (ext), so ξ̃(x) = e, σ(x) = 1 and ξ(x)(α) = α(E_ι) = σ(x)·α(E_ι).
   (b) If ξ(x)(β) = −β(E_ι) for all β, then ξ̃(x) = ξ(x) = −e. If moreover ξ̃(x) = e, then σ(x) = 1 and ξ(x)(α) = ξ̃(x)(α) = e(α) = α(E_ι) = σ(x)·α(E_ι). Otherwise σ(x) = −1 and ξ(x)(α) = −α(E_ι) = σ(x)·α(E_ι).
   So ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(E_ι) for every α, for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: (IMC-b) restricts R to M ∩ E with the same orientation; R'.orients gives approximate tangent planes Q of M ∩ E oriented by ξ(x), a.e. on M ∩ E.
Points of M ∩ E agree with x off range ι, so (PO) gives ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(E_ι)) a.e. on M ∩ E.
With ξ̃ a strongly measurable version of ξ and e = evaluation at E_ι, σ := 1 on {ξ̃ = e}, −1 on {ξ̃ ≠ e, ξ̃ = −e}, 0 elsewhere is Borel with |σ| ≤ 1.
Case analysis on ξ(x) = ±e gives ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)α(E_ι) a.e.

audit.reason: Both universal antecedents and all local hypotheses match the prose. Restriction supplies tangent orientations, PO gives the two signs, and a strongly measurable representative yields a Borel integer-valued sign. The proof preserves the simultaneous quantifier over all covectors and handles coincident sign cases. The supplied topology instance was independently validated.

subproblem.title: Only finitely many unit lattice faces meet a compact set (parent step 5)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and K ⊆ ℝ^P compact. Then only finitely many index pairs p = (ι, b), with ι : Fin k → Fin P arbitrary and b ∈ ℤ^P, have Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} ∈ K for some y in the closed unit cube [0,1]^k (in Lean: the set {p | ∃ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) 1 ∈ K} is finite).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → {p : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) | ∃ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ) ∈ K}.Finite
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the finiteness part of step 5 of the parent proof (only finitely many unit lattice faces meet the compact set K); the bound is written for an arbitrary (not necessarily injective) ι and the closed cube.

Notation: e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and Φ_p as in the statement; coordinate formula Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + S_i with S_i := Σ_j y_j·[i = ι(j)] (Pi.single_apply).

1. (K is bounded.) K is compact, hence bounded, so there is ρ ∈ ℝ with ‖x‖ ≤ ρ for all x ∈ K (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.exists_norm_le). For every x ∈ ℝ^P and every i, |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
2. (The coordinate shift is between 0 and k.) If y ∈ [0,1]^k then 0 ≤ S_i ≤ k for every i: each summand is y_j·1 ∈ [0,1] or y_j·0 = 0, and there are k summands.
3. (Bounds on b.) Let p = (ι, b) be in the set, witnessed by y ∈ [0,1]^k with x := Φ_p(y) ∈ K. For each i, |b_i + S_i| = |x_i| ≤ ρ. Put N := ⌈ρ⌉ + k ∈ ℤ. Then b_i ≤ ρ − S_i ≤ ρ ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ ≤ N, and b_i ≥ −ρ − S_i ≥ −ρ − k ≥ −⌈ρ⌉ − k = −N (Int.le_ceil). So b_i ∈ [−N, N] for every i.
4. (Finiteness.) By step 3 the set is contained in univ ×ˢ (univ.pi fun _ => Icc (−N) N) ⊆ (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ). The first factor is a finite type, and the second is a finite product of finite integer intervals (Set.Finite.pi, Set.finite_Icc). Hence the product is finite (Set.Finite.prod), and so is its subset (Set.Finite.subset). ∎
proof_key_steps: K compact gives ρ with |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ ≤ ρ on K.
For y ∈ [0,1]^k, Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + S_i with 0 ≤ S_i ≤ k, so |b_i| ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ + k.
The set lies in (all ι) × (integer box [−N, N]^P), a finite set.

audit.reason: The contract correctly permits arbitrary direction maps. Bounding each coordinate shift between 0 and k bounds the integer base points in a finite box. The finite-product argument proves the stated finiteness without an omitted injectivity hypothesis.

subproblem.title: A point of the (m+1)-skeleton off the m-skeleton lies on an open unit lattice (m+1)-face (parent step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P). Assume (i) x ∈ L_{m+1}: there is a set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s; and (ii) x ∉ L_m: there is no set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s. Then x lies on an open unit lattice (m+1)-face: there are a strictly increasing ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P, b ∈ ℤ^P and y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with 0 < y_j < 1 for every j such that x = b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (in Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 = x, with p = (ι, b)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (x : Euclid P), (∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z) → (¬ ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z) → ∃ (p : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ)) (y : Euclid (m + 1)), StrictMono p.1 ∧ (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ) = x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1: points of the n-skeleton off the (n−1)-skeleton lie in open n-faces), with the cardinality and coordinate bookkeeping written out.

Notation: e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1; for p = (ι, b), Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • e_{ι j}. Coordinate formula (EuclideanSpace.single_apply / Pi.single_apply, used throughout): Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j y_j·[i = ι(j)].

1. (Integer coordinates.) Let J := {i ∈ Fin P : ∃ z ∈ ℤ, x_i = z}, a Finset (Finset.univ.filter).
2. (Upper bound on P.) By (i) choose s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s. Then s ⊆ J, hence |s| ≤ |J| (Finset.card_le_card) and P ≤ m + 1 + |J|.
3. (Lower bound on P.) Every i ∈ J has x_i ∈ ℤ, so if P ≤ m + |J| held, s := J would contradict (ii). Hence m + |J| < P.
4. (Exactly m + 1 free coordinates.) By 2 and 3, P = m + 1 + |J|. The complement Jᶜ in Fin P has |Jᶜ| = P − |J| = m + 1 (Finset.card_compl, Fintype.card_fin; omega).
5. (The direction map.) Let ι := Jᶜ.orderEmbOfFin h : Fin (m+1) ↪o Fin P, h the cardinality equation of step 4. It is strictly increasing (OrderEmbedding.strictMono), ι(j) ∈ Jᶜ for every j (Finset.orderEmbOfFin_mem), and range ι = Jᶜ (Finset.range_orderEmbOfFin).
6. (The base point and parameters.) Put b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ for every i, y := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => Int.fract (x_{ι(j)})), and p := (ι, b).
7. (y lies in the open cube.) Int.fract (x_{ι(j)}) < 1 always (Int.fract_lt_one). Since ι(j) ∉ J, x_{ι(j)} is not an integer, in particular x_{ι(j)} ≠ ⌊x_{ι(j)}⌋, so Int.fract (x_{ι(j)}) > 0 (Int.fract_pos). Hence 0 < y_j < 1 for every j.
8. (Φ_p(y) = x, coordinatewise.) Fix i.
   (a) If i ∈ J, then i ∉ range ι, so every summand y_j·[i = ι(j)] vanishes and Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋. As x_i = z ∈ ℤ, ⌊x_i⌋ = z = x_i.
   (b) If i ∉ J, then i ∈ Jᶜ = range ι, say i = ι(j₀); since ι is injective, [ι(j₀) = ι(j)] holds only for j = j₀, so the sum is y_{j₀} = Int.fract x_i and Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ + Int.fract x_i = x_i (Int.floor_add_fract).
   Hence Φ_p(y) = x (ext over i), and p, y satisfy all requirements. ∎
proof_key_steps: J := {i : x_i ∈ ℤ}; (i) gives P ≤ m + 1 + |J| and (ii) with s = J gives m + |J| < P, so |Jᶜ| = m + 1.
ι := orderEmbOfFin of Jᶜ (strictly increasing, range Jᶜ), b := ⌊x⌋, y_j := fract(x_{ι(j)}) ∈ (0,1) since x_{ι(j)} ∉ ℤ.
Coordinatewise, Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ = x_i for i ∈ J and ⌊x_i⌋ + fract(x_i) = x_i for i = ι(j₀); so Φ_p(y) = x.

subproblem.title: On one open lattice face an integer multiplicity current is an integer L^1 density (Simon (33); parent steps 8, 10-12 per face)
subproblem.statement: Assume (IMC-b) [the second conjunct of the frozen hypothesis (IMC) of the parent]: for all P, n, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R in U and every set E, if U is open and E is Borel then there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with R' representing A, R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient, and (PO) [the exact frozen type of the sibling Submission.cmcdtfr_plane_orientation]: for all P, n, strictly increasing ι : Fin n → Fin P, A ⊆ ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, linear subspaces Q ⊆ ℝ^P and n-vectors ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P n, if a_i = x_i for every a ∈ A and every i ∉ range ι, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, then either ξ(α) = α(E_ι) for every n-covector α or ξ(α) = −α(E_ι) for every α, where E_ι := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}). Let P, n ∈ ℕ, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n), and p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing and b ∈ ℤ^P, such that Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1) is an isometry ℝ^n → ℝ^P. Let Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝ^n : 0 < y_i < 1 ∀ i}, F̆ := Φ_p(Q₁) and E_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}). Then there is u : ℝ^n → ℝ such that u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y, u is integrable on Q₁ (Lebesgue measure), ENNReal.ofReal(∫_{Q₁} |u|) ≤ R.measure(F̆) (= ∫_{M∩F̆} θ dHⁿ), and for every test n-form ω on ℝ^P (TestFormOn univ n): ∫_{M ∩ F̆} θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{Q₁} u(y) ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 8, 10, 11 and 12 of the parent proof restricted to one face (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, display (33): Q⌞F̆ is an integer density on the face F̆), with the face orientation of step 9 supplied by the sibling child coordinate_plane_orientation_sign.

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Φ := Φ_p; e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1; c := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)); vol := Lebesgue measure (volume) on Euclid n.

1. (Measurability.) Q₁ = ⋂_i ({y : 0 < y_i} ∩ {y : y_i < 1}) is Borel, the coordinate maps y ↦ y_i being continuous (EuclideanSpace.proj). Φ is an isometry, hence a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding) and therefore a measurable embedding (IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). So F̆ = Φ(Q₁) is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image'), and so is M ∩ F̆.
2. (F̆ lies in a coordinate plane.) For a = Φ(y) and an index i with ι(j) ≠ i for all j, a_i = b_i + Σ_j y_j·(e_{ι(j)})_i = b_i + 0 = c_i (Pi.single_apply).
3. (Orientation sign.) Apply the sibling child coordinate_plane_orientation_sign (the antecedents (IMC-b) and (PO) are those of this statement) to P, n, U := univ (open), R, ι, c, E := F̆, using ι strictly increasing, F̆ Borel (step 1) and step 2. It gives a Borel σ : ℝ^P → ℤ with |σ| ≤ 1 such that for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ F̆)-a.e. x: ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(E_p) for every α.
4. (Change of variables.) Hⁿ = vol on Euclid n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and Φ is an isometry, so map Φ vol = Hⁿ⌞(range Φ) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). Since F̆ ⊆ range Φ and Φ⁻¹(F̆) = Q₁ (Φ injective):
   Hⁿ⌞F̆ = (Hⁿ⌞range Φ)⌞F̆ = (map Φ vol)⌞F̆ = map Φ (vol⌞Q₁)
   (Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, Function.Injective.preimage_image). Hence for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{F̆} f dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} f(Φ(y)) dy (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map), and for every f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{F̆} f dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{Q₁} f(Φ(y)) dy (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). Neither identity needs measurability or integrability of f.
5. (The density.) Let g := M.indicator (x ↦ θ(x)·σ(x)), h := M.indicator (x ↦ θ(x)) (real valued) and u(y) := g(Φ(y)).
   (a) g is Borel: θ is measurable, every map out of ℕ or ℤ is measurable (so the casts to ℝ are measurable), σ is Borel and M is Borel (Measurable.indicator). Φ is continuous, so u is Borel.
   (b) u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y: u(y) = θ(Φ(y))·σ(Φ(y)) ∈ ℤ if Φ(y) ∈ M, and u(y) = 0 otherwise.
   (c) |g(x)| ≤ h(x) for every x: for x ∈ M, |θ(x)σ(x)| = θ(x)|σ(x)| ≤ θ(x) since θ ≥ 0 and |σ| ≤ 1; for x ∉ M both sides are 0.
6. (Face mass.) ofReal ∘ h = M.indicator (x ↦ (θ(x) : [0,∞])). Hence ∫⁻_{F̆} ofReal(h) dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M ∩ F̆} θ dHⁿ = ((Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ)(F̆) = R.measure(F̆) (lintegral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict, withDensity_apply with F̆ Borel, IMRep.measure).
7. (Finiteness.) C := WithLp.toLp 2 '' (∏_i [0,1]) is compact (isCompact_univ_pi, isCompact_Icc, continuity of WithLp.toLp), K := Φ(C) is compact (Φ continuous) and Borel, and F̆ ⊆ K (y = WithLp.toLp 2 (WithLp.ofLp y) with WithLp.ofLp y ∈ ∏_i [0,1]). So R.measure(F̆) ≤ R.measure(K) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult K (K compact, K ⊆ univ).
8. (Integrability and the mass bound.) ‖u(y)‖ₑ = ofReal|u(y)| ≤ ofReal(h(Φ(y))) by 5(c), so ∫⁻_{Q₁} ‖u‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{Q₁} ofReal(h ∘ Φ) = ∫⁻_{F̆} ofReal(h) dHⁿ = R.measure(F̆) < ∞ (steps 4, 6, 7). With 5(a), u is integrable on Q₁.
